Account.description: An account: a node that holds assets. Currency (ISO 4217) is the currency the account is kept in: its transaction lines' amounts and its holdings' market values are in it, as its institution reports them.

AccountConnection.description: Links an account to the same account at its source: the broker's account number, or the aggregator's account ID.

Alert.description: A compliance violation found by the rules: one per node and rule, removed when the rule is satisfied again.

Asset.description: Anything that can be held: cash, a stock, a fund, a bond, an option, a future or a coin. Its identity is a node, its Symbol rows are its names in each scheme (Currency, Ticker, Cusip), and one extension table by asset type holds what is particular to it. Its price is quoted in QuoteCurrency (ISO 4217; a currency is quoted in itself, at 1). Market value in an account's currency is quantity × QuantityFactor × price × PriceFactor × the price of QuoteCurrency in the account's currency: QuantityFactor is the units one quantity stands for (100 shares for an option, a futures contract's multiplier), PriceFactor the units a quoted price stands for (0.01 for a bond priced per 100 of face value, or a future quoted in cents).

Cash.description: An asset of type Cash: a currency, held in units of itself at a price of one.

Crypto.description: An asset of type Crypto: a coin or token on a blockchain.

Equity.description: An asset of type Equity: a share in a company.

FixedIncome.description: An asset of type Fixed Income: a bond or note. Quantity is face value; price is per 100 of face value.

Fund.description: An asset of type Fund: a share in a pooled vehicle (an exchange-traded fund, a mutual fund, a money market fund).

Future.description: An asset of type Future: an agreement to buy or sell its underlying at a set price on its expiration date.

Option.description: An asset of type Option: the right to buy (call) or sell (put) its underlying asset at the strike price until it expires.

Price.description: The latest price of a symbol in a currency: the price of one unit of what the symbol names, as quoted, in units of Currency (NVDA in USD; USD in USD, which is 1; USD in GBP). Published by the market data feed and, for constants such as a currency's price in itself, from the server's initial prices at startup. Ticks are ephemeral: never persisted, synced, or served by the API.

PriceOverride.description: An event: the operator sets an asset's price from its effective time until it expires, because a source has it wrong.

TargetWeight.description: The customer's specification of an account: each asset's share of the account's value, as of a date (a published methodology's weights for that day, for instance). Recorded once per date and never changed; the latest date on or before the trading day is the one in force, and an asset it leaves out is to be sold. What the weights don't add up to stays in cash.

RebalanceSetting.description: How an account is rebalanced: once a trading day, at TimeOfDay (minutes after midnight in New York) or later, on weekdays only unless WeekdaysOnly is false; a trade smaller than Band (a fraction of the account's value) is skipped; orders go to Broker. No setting, no rebalancing.

Rebalance.description: A rebalance the rules decided: one per account and trading day, recorded with the orders it created (OrderCount, possibly none), so the account is rebalanced once that day however often the rules run.

CancelRequest.description: A request to cancel a broker order. The router sends it while the order is still open at the broker; the broker's report (cancelled, or the fills that beat it) says what happened.

Order.description: An order: an intention to buy or sell one asset, for one or more accounts (its allocations). Recorded once and never changed; its status is derived from its broker orders and their execution reports. Origin says what created it (with RuleName for a rule).

Allocation.description: One account's share of an order: the quantity of the order's asset it is to buy or sell. The order's quantity is the sum of its allocations. Fills are booked to the allocations in proportion to what each still needs, in whole units, by a published deterministic rule.

BrokerOrder.description: An order as sent to a broker for execution: part or all of an order (an order may be split into several). BrokerOrderId is the ID the broker is given, so a retried send is the same order. Recorded once and never changed; its status comes from the broker's execution reports.

ExecutionReport.description: What a broker reported about a broker order: accepted, a fill (a quantity at a price, with fees), cancelled, rejected or expired. Recorded once, idempotently on the broker's own ID for the report (Source, SourceId), and never changed. The rules book each fill to the order's accounts as Buy or Sell transactions.

Transaction.description: An event: something that happened at a time, recorded once and never changed (a mistake is corrected by another transaction). One atomic unit: its lines are inserted with it, in the same batch. An exchange (a purchase or a sale) gives one asset for another, so its lines balance. A temporary entry (an override) carries ExpiresTime and is in force from its effective time until then.

TransactionLine.description: What a transaction does to one holding: an account's quantity of one asset. Effect Change adds Quantity (negative to remove); Effect SetTo sets it (an override). Amount is the line's value in the account's currency at the transaction: what was received (positive) or given (negative); for a purchase, the cost; null when unknown. RelatedAssetId names another asset the line is about (the company that paid a dividend).
